display.purpose: The room code only — 2.4rem bold monospace, 0.35em tracking.

headline.purpose: The POWER HUNGRY PETS wordmark — printed masthead tracking.

title.purpose: One uppercase slip title per slip, never stacked.

body.purpose: All sentences on paper; slips stay narrow enough to skip a measure clamp.

hint.purpose: Supporting sentences: statuses, recovery copy, empty states.

label.purpose: Rubber-stamped field labels and slip section headers.

tag.purpose: HOST and presence chips — the smallest stamped voice.

motion.name: reduced-motion-policy
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce -> transition: none !important; animation: none !important; slip tilt: none
motion.purpose: No transitions or animations are authored; states change instantly. The reduced-motion block exists to strip slip rotation and any future motion.

gameplayLayer.name: Digital Tabletop Arcade (gameplay layer)
gameplayLayer.purpose: From match start the interface becomes a digital tabletop arcade: the table is the protagonist, cards are large, players sit around the table as avatars, the current action happens at the table's center, and mandatory private decisions appear in a centered modal over the inert table.
compositionRules: The table owns the screen's center; administrative content stays minimal at the edges.
Cards are the biggest interactive objects at a 63:88 proportion; opponent hands read as face-down backs per seat.

Mandatory private decisions (Pecera target/guess, Saqueadog keep/swap, Ratón reinsertion) render in a centered modal: table visible but inert, focus trapped, Escape and outside clicks never dismiss it.
Warm physical feel, no HUD: no sci-fi chrome, no glassmorphism; soft physical shadows are deferred to Milestone 8.
gameplayLayer.m7Boundary: Through Milestone 7 this layer governs composition only — no final artwork, textures, branded card frames, background art, or animation; placeholders and stable asset keys remain the standing seam for Milestone 8 polish.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: At or below 46rem, side-by-side slip arrangements stack into a single column in reading order.

components.name: Paper Slip with Pin
components.description: The signature container: a cream paper slip pinned to the dark board, tilted slightly, square-cornered with a 1px ink border.
components.html:
Tonight's invitation

Every content region on the board is a slip.

components.name: Action Button
components.description: Printed-paper button: paper face, 2px ink border, 3rem minimum height; hover lifts to raised paper, disabled goes dashed and faded.

<button type="button" class="ds-btn">Pin a new room</button>
<button type="button" class="ds-btn" disabled>Pinning the room…</button>
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-block; min-height: 3rem; min-width: 3rem; padding: 0.55rem 1.3rem; font: inherit; font-family: 'Iowan Old Style', 'Palatino Linotype', Palatino, Georgia, serif; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: var(--paper-ink, #22312c); background: var(--paper, #f2e7cf); border: 2px solid var(--paper-ink, #22312c); border-radius: 2px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--paper-raised, #fffaf0); } .ds-btn:disabled { border-style: dashed; opacity: 0.55; cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-btn:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--enamel-yellow, #f1b94b); outline: 3px solid var(--paper-ink, #22312c); outline-offset: 2px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-btn { transition: none; } }

components.name: Connection Line
components.description: One serif sentence whose colored underline confirms state: yellow when connected, coral when disconnected or erroring, plain when idle. The words inform; the rule confirms.
components.html:
At the game noticeboard.

The line to the board dropped — reconnecting…
components.css: .ds-connection-line { margin: 0; font-family: 'Iowan Old Style', 'Palatino Linotype', Palatino, Georgia, serif; font-size: 0.95rem; letter-spacing: 0.03em; color: var(--paper, #f2e7cf); } .ds-connection-line[data-connection='connected'] { border-bottom: 2px solid var(--enamel-yellow, #f1b94b); display: inline-block; padding-bottom: 0.1rem; } .ds-connection-line[data-connection='disconnected'], .ds-connection-line[data-connection='error'] { border-bottom: 2px solid var(--coral, #e05a3f); display: inline-block; padding-bottom: 0.1rem; }

narrative.overview:
The interface is a dark community noticeboard. Every screen is a cork-green board; every piece of content is a printed paper slip pinned to it with an enamel pin. A room begins as one large, slightly tilted invitation slip — the player's name, the room code, the actions — and guests arrive as further name slips gathering around it in real time. Nothing is a floating panel: content is physically attached to the board, the way a convocation flyer is attached to a neighborhood corkboard.

The system is deliberately printed and tactile. Forms are printed-paper forms: heavy small-caps labels stamped above ruled fields, flat ink-bordered buttons, monospaced room codes set like hand-stamped serials. Depth comes from physical affordances — a tilted slip, a pin head, a lighter paper field — never from glow, glass, or shadow. Color is scarce on purpose: the board is dark, the paper is warm, and the only saturated hues (coral, enamel yellow) are reserved for status, connection, and focus.

Every interaction answers textually and immediately: buttons rename themselves while busy, copy outcomes print a sentence, connection state reads as a line of text with a colored underline. Hover is never load-bearing; the interface must work one-handed on a phone, from a touch target, without any pointer resting on it.
keyCharacteristics: Dark cork-green board (#17332d) as the only page ground; cream paper (#f2e7cf) as the content voice.
Flat bordered paper slips with enamel pins; no gradients, no glass, no equal-card grids.
Coral (#e05a3f) and enamel yellow (#f1b94b) reserved for error/connection/focus/selection — never decoration.
Heavy uppercase labels with wide tracking; monospace only for room codes.
Depth by pin and tilt (±0.7°), not shadow; focus is the only box-shadow on the page.
Textual confirmation for every action; hover is never required.
3rem minimum interactive height; slips destack and untilt under prefers-reduced-motion.

rules.name: The Status-Only Color Rule
rules.body: Coral and enamel yellow never decorate. They mark error, connection state, keyboard focus, and selection — and nothing else. If a hue appears without a state behind it, it is a defect.

rules.name: The Rubber-Stamp Label Rule
rules.body: Labels are small, bold, widely tracked uppercase set in the same serif as the body — they read as stamped headings, not as a sans-serif UI font dropped in from another world.

rules.name: The Pin, Not the Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth is expressed by what attaches a slip to the board — the enamel pin and the ±0.7° tilt — never by cast light. Shadows are for focus only.

dos: Do reserve coral (#e05a3f) and enamel yellow (#f1b94b) for error, connection, focus, and selection states — per the Status-Only Color Rule.
Do answer every action textually: busy labels ("Pinning the room…"), status sentences, and connection lines. The board speaks.
Do keep interactive targets at least 3rem tall; hover is never required to reach any state.
Do keep keyboard focus doubly visible: 0 0 0 2px Enamel Yellow ring plus a 3px Paper Ink outline at 2px offset.
Do tilt slips subtly (±0.7° max) and drop all tilt and motion under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do use dashed borders for provisional things: disabled actions, empty slots, notice separators.
Do use Coral Ink (#a3341f), not Coral, for any alarm-colored text on paper (5.6:1).
donts: Don't add gradients, glassmorphism, or drop shadows; the board is flat and depth comes from pins and tilt.
Don't invent a ninth color; the palette is closed at eight tokens.
Don't arrange content into equal-card grids of identical tiles; slips differ by role, tilt, and content.
Don't rely on color alone to carry status — every state also has text or a label.
Don't set the monospace voice anywhere except room codes (typed and displayed).
Don't round corners beyond 2px or make pill shapes; paper is cut, not molded.
Don't let animation imply game state; presentation may animate authorized events but never determines them.
